segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Again he began to teach beside the sea. And a very large crowd gathered around him, so that he got into a boat and sat in it on the sea, while the whole crowd was on the land beside the sea.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He taught them many things in parables, and in his teaching he said to them:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Listen! Look, a sower went out to sow.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And as he sowed, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and ate it up.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Other seed fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil, and it sprang up at once because it had no depth of soil;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and when the sun rose it was scorched, and because it had no root it withered.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it, and it yielded no crop.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And other seeds fell into the good soil and yielded a crop, coming up and growing, and produced one thirtyfold, one sixtyfold, and one a hundredfold.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he was alone, those around him, together with the Twelve, asked him about the parables.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “To you the secret of the kingdom of God has been given; but to those outside, everything comes in parables,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: so that ‘they may look and look yet not see, and hear and hear yet not understand; otherwise they might turn back and be forgiven.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You do not grasp this parable? Then how will you understand all the parables?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The sower sows the word.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: These are the ones along the path, where the word is sown: when they hear, at once Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And these, likewise, are the ones sown on the rocky ground: when they hear the word, they at once receive it with joy,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: yet they have no root in themselves and last only a while; then, when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, at once they fall away.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And others are the ones sown among the thorns. These are the ones who have heard the word,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but the worries of the age and the deceitfulness of wealth and the desires for everything else come in and choke the word, and it bears no crop.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And those are the ones sown on the good soil: they hear the word and accept it and bear a crop, one thirtyfold, one sixtyfold, and one a hundredfold.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Is a lamp brought in to be put under the grain measure or under the bed? Is it not to be put on the lampstand?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For nothing is hidden except to be brought to light, and nothing was concealed except to come to light.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If anyone has ears to hear, let them hear!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Pay attention to what you hear. By the measure you measure with, it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For whoever has will be given more; and whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken away from them.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The kingdom of God is like this: as if a man were to cast seed on the ground

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and sleep and rise, night and day, while the seed sprouts and grows tall, he himself does not know how.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: On its own the ground bears a crop: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But when the crop is ready, at once he sends in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “How shall we picture the kingdom of God, or in what parable shall we put it?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: It is like a mustard seed, which, when it is sown on the ground, is smaller than all the seeds on the earth—

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: yet when it is sown, it comes up and becomes larger than all the garden plants and puts out large branches, so that the birds of the sky can nest under its shade.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as far as they were able to hear it;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he did not speak to them without a parable, but privately, to his own disciples, he explained everything.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On that day, when evening had come, he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Let us cross over to the other side.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And leaving the crowd, they took him along in the boat, just as he was; and other boats were with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And a great windstorm arose, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already filling.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he himself was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion. And they woke him and said to him,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he woke up, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Quiet! Be silent!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the wind died down, and there was a great calm.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why are you such cowards? Do you still have no faith?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they were seized with a great fear and said to one another,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

notes.note: This is the Sea of Galilee, a freshwater lake about thirteen miles long. Mark calls it a 'sea', following Semitic usage in which one word covers any large body of water; Luke prefers 'lake'. 'Sea' is kept because the word carries weight at the end of the chapter, where the scene recalls Old Testament language about God ruling the sea.

notes.traditional: some thirtyfold, some sixty, some a hundred
notes.note: The earliest manuscripts were written without accents or breathing marks, so the same letters can be read as 'one' or as the preposition 'in', and some manuscripts have a different preposition altogether. The edition translated here reads 'one … one … one', probably reflecting an Aramaic idiom for '-fold'. The sense is not materially affected.

The older English rendering is 'mystery', which now suggests a puzzle or something inherently unknowable. In period usage, including the Greek version of Daniel, the word means something hidden that God has disclosed to chosen recipients. Many modern translations likewise use 'secret'.

The Greek conjunction most naturally expresses purpose, and the text is translated that way. Some interpreters take it as result ('with the result that') or as shorthand for 'so that the scripture might be fulfilled', and the word rendered 'otherwise' can also mean 'unless perhaps'. The question is much disputed; the parallel in Matthew 13:13 has 'because' instead.

notes.phrase: they may look and look yet not see
notes.note: Jesus adapts Isaiah 6:9–10, where the prophet is told his preaching will meet with incomprehension. The closing words 'be forgiven' differ from the Septuagint's 'I will heal them' and agree with the Aramaic paraphrase of Isaiah used in synagogues. The doubled verbs reproduce a Hebrew idiom of emphasis.

The Greek word denotes a span of time, here the present era of human history as contrasted with the age to come, rather than the physical world. Most translations have 'world' or 'this life'. 'Age' keeps the temporal sense a first-century Jewish hearer would have recognised.

The word is a borrowing of the Latin modius, a household vessel for measuring dry goods that held roughly eight or nine litres. The traditional 'bushel' names a measure about four times that size and no longer suggests a container to most readers. Modern translations vary between 'basket' and 'bowl'.

The wording echoes Joel 3:13 (4:13 in the Greek numbering), 'Send in the sickle, for the harvest has come', a picture of God's final judgment. A hearer who knew the prophets would catch that the parable's harvest points to the end of the age.

notes.phrase: the birds of the sky can nest under its shade
notes.traditional: the birds of the air can make nests in its shade
notes.note: The image recalls Ezekiel 17:23 and 31:6 and Daniel 4:12, where a great tree sheltering birds stands for a kingdom that gives protection to many peoples. 'Birds of the heaven' is a standing Semitic phrase for wild birds; the visible sky is meant.

The traditional wording sounds soothing, but the Greek is a pair of sharp commands to stop making noise. The second verb is used in the period both for muzzling an animal and for silencing a person, and it is the one Jesus uses to silence the unclean spirit in 1:25. Its form here implies 'be silenced and stay so'.

The adjective means cowardly or timid and is a term of reproach, a different word from the ordinary one for fear used in the next verse. Most translations render 'afraid' or 'fearful', which blurs the distinction between the disciples' loss of nerve in the storm and their awe afterwards.
